gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much energy per pound a specific power bank carries, or how much energy the usual two-bank airline limit lets you board with: 2 × 99.75 Wh = 199.5 Wh weighing 1.32 kg (2.64 lb) with Anker's Prime 26K, against 2 × 72 Wh = 144 Wh weighing 582 g (1.28 lb) with Nitecore's NB20000 Gen3, which at 112 Wh/lb carries about 1.5× the energy per pound of the Prime 26K's 75.6 Wh/lb.
standout_why: I read RuntimeWise's airline-rules page (result 16). It gives airline limits on watt-hours and on how many power banks you may carry, plus capacities for generic mAh sizes. It has no figures for real products, such as Wh per pound, cost per Wh or total energy under the bank-count limit. ChatGPT's own answer only converts mAh to Wh at 3.7 V and gives no weights. I could not read the cited IATA PDF (the fetch returned unreadable compressed bytes, and its metadata names a wheelchair guidance document). The cited aa.com page and the uncited FAA PackSafe page both returned HTTP 403, so I could not confirm what they leave out. Those are the pages ChatGPT cited, so the score rests on RuntimeWise and ChatGPT's own answer.
decides: Many airlines cap you at two power banks, and RuntimeWise lists seven, Emirates included, that ban recharging a bank from seat power. The energy you board with is therefore close to all you get, so total Wh within the bank limit, and its weight, is the number that matters. For phones and tablets, the Nitecore NB20000 Gen3 gives the most energy per pound among the banks I could source (two of them: 144 Wh for 582 g). For laptops, two Anker Prime 26K banks reach the highest total, 199.5 Wh, but cost 618 g more for 55.5 Wh more. On Emirates (one bank), the best you can carry is the Prime 26K's 99.75 Wh. The finding backs a split pick: a light high-density bank for phones and a 99.75 Wh bank for laptops. It does not support ChatGPT's single answer of a 20,000 mAh bank.

findings.note: Per-airline notes (RuntimeWise read the airlines' pages on 2026-10-22). Banned from seat or aircraft power: American, BA, Emirates, Qantas. Banned outright on board: Delta, JetBlue, Ryanair. Cathay, Korean, Lufthansa, Qatar and Singapore ban use and charging, or charging alone, so they likely also bar charging from seat power, though their notes don't name it. The point: the energy you board with is close to all you get.
